tasks.text: Read issue/plan/amendments and code (core event, log payload/projection)
Commit 1: kinds + payloads + thread_started fields + ignore arms + T1-T4
Commit 2: RunState + NextMove + LogError::RunOrdering + amendment-2 tests
Gate: fmt, clippy --all-targets, full test suite (900s, logged)
Post ## Implementation report with test ledger

data.reasoning_content:
Wait, this commit message mentions Amendment 2 specifics (Verdict without Fix, FixSize, u32 version, slots JSON, no size, budget_usd) — good, that's what I wrote in commit 1 (I wrote /tmp/msg1.txt with that body; I recall it was a long body). OK. But `crates/log/src/lib.rs` in commit 1 holds only payload exports; the run_state exports are in commit 2. And store.rs's `RunOrdering` variant is in commit 2 — fine (commit 1 compiled without them; store.rs change appearing after commit 1 means commit 1 didn't include it).

Hmm, but wait: commit 1 included lib.rs's payload exports — that's fine.

Actually hold on: was `LogError::RunOrdering` in commit 1's store.rs? git status after commit 1 showed `M crates/log/src/store.rs` — meaning the store.rs edit came after commit 1. Good.

Let me double check commit 1 compiles standalone? It was committed after a successful clippy run over the tree at that time... The clippy run before commit 1 was `cargo clippy --all-targets` — at that moment lib.rs did not export run_state (I had removed it) and store.rs had no RunOrdering. Actually no: the RunOrdering variant and store.rs edits happened in the *second* batch, after commit 1. And the clippy run right before commit 1 passed. So commit 1 is self-consistent. Good enough (bisectability is nice-to-have).

Now the gate.
